source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA and FAA references on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed current NASA technical planning, product verification, V&V plan, software verification planning/test estimation, HSI planning, and NPR requirements; FAA lifecycle V&V and service-requirement matrix guidance; and NASA/SP-2016-6105 Rev. 2. Agency-specific requirements are attributed and not generalized as universal compliance rules.

evidence: Reviewed per-requirement verification record V_r=(B,M,L,A,C,P,O,E,D).
Reviewed requirement-to-activity trace relation, activity method/level/article/condition/resource/duration/dependency/oracle/risk notation.
Reviewed conditional evidence-credit notation and state distinctions among mapped, feasible, ready, executed, and closed.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation organizes plan accountability and does not imply that a filled row is feasible, adequate, or closed.

evidence: Executed verification-plan-readiness-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-072/report.json.
Confirmed five mapped rows use four distinct methods and initially only three unique rows are ready.
Confirmed blockers REQ-004:missing_oracle and REQ-005:facility_unavailable.
Confirmed both corrections yield five ready rows and no declared structural blocker.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Boolean structural checks do not assess technical adequacy, capacity, schedule feasibility, configuration, uncertainty, or actual compliance.

evidence: Confirmed row mapping is necessary but does not imply readiness, execution, or closure.
Confirmed lower-level and heritage evidence credit is conditional rather than automatically transitive.
Confirmed method, level, article, conditions, and oracle must form one coherent inference path.
Confirmed schedule compression cannot remove logical prerequisites or evidence/disposition states.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The planning model describes necessary evidence relationships, not a theorem that field completeness proves correctness.

evidence: Challenged missing oracles, unavailable facilities/external systems, destructive unique articles, hidden observables, and unrepresentative configurations.
Reviewed interface, timing, overload, fault/degraded/recovery, human, software/data, cyber, maintenance, and common-cause claims.
Reviewed model/simulator credibility, measurement uncertainty, finite sampling, supplier/COTS/heritage credit, and production equivalence.
Reviewed readiness, abort, anomaly, invalid-run, waiver, regression, retest, emergency release, and operational-change governance.
Reviewed resource contention, long leads, calibration, logistics, analysis/report capacity, and risk-shaped reserves.
Reviewed all ten examples and five answers for assumptions, reasoning, evidence limits, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real plans require domain, requirements, architecture, integration, test, facilities, configuration/data, statistics/metrology, model/simulation, human-factors, safety/security, supplier, quality, regulatory, independent review, technical-authority, and acceptance input as applicable.

evidence: Confirmed every requirement needs an adequate evidence path and every activity a justified claim or learning objective.
Confirmed requirement/product/tool/data/procedure/result configurations remain bound.
Confirmed evidence composition preserves interface, emergence, assumption, limitation, and configuration conditions.
Confirmed resources and schedule cover preparation through analysis, anomaly, correction, regression, retest, report, and closure.
Confirmed qualification, verification, validation, acceptance, certification, developmental work, and regression remain distinct.
Confirmed waiver/deviation does not rewrite technical nonconformance and changes trigger selective re-verification.
invariant_checking.notes: No matrix percentage, method label, booked date, supplier certificate, automated pass rate, waiver, or prior qualification is presented as sufficient closure evidence.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents planning structures and conditional inference rules but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled synthetic_structural_readiness_only and disclaims technical sufficiency.
Official guidance is attributed without claiming local compliance, readiness, verification, certification, or approval.
Planned activities are distinguished from executed evidence and closed requirements.
No external review or operational verification result is claimed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic structure, source-backed planning guidance, internal review, and real verification assurance remain separated.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked strategy, plan, matrix, method, level, article, enabling product, qualification, acceptance, closure, evidence credit, readiness, configuration, and re-verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked scope/authority, verification architecture, method/level/article/oracle selection, facilities and people, integration, risk, resource/dependency schedule, readiness, evidence management, anomalies, closure, credit, regression, automation, and forecasts.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from per-requirement claims through executable planning and governance. Ten distinct examples and five complete solutions cover physical, software, service, supplier, simulation, resource, automation, and change cases.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/FAA expert, regulator, customer, requirements or architecture owner, integration or test engineer, facility or metrology authority, model/simulation specialist, statistician, human-factors specialist, safety/security engineer, supplier, configuration/data/quality authority, independent V&V reviewer, technical authority, acceptance authority, or certification body review is claimed.
